{'index': 0, 'translation': 'Despite facing a second lawsuit over the theft of trade secrets related to its hardware business in just over a year, OpenAI still plans to unveil its first product later this year and officially launch it in 2027. According to Bloomberg, here are the details.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'First Product Reveal Still Scheduled for 2026'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': "Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company and several former Apple employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer device business."}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'The complaint detailed what it called a "pattern of Apple former employees stealing Apple trade secrets during their tenure at OpenAI," and stated that "such misconduct has become routine, and has been tacitly approved and exemplified by management."'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': "This lawsuit further escalates OpenAI's legal troubles regarding its hardware business. Previously, the startup iyO had already filed a lawsuit over branding matters, and later amended its complaint to include allegations of trade secret theft."}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'Despite the lawsuit news emerging last Friday, OpenAI appears to be sticking to its hardware timeline for now. According to Bloomberg:'}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'Since OpenAI announced its partnership with Jony Ive\'s io Products to develop an "AI-first" device, there have been many speculations circulating about what exactly OpenAI has planned.'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': "Shortly after the partnership was announced in May 2025, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo immediately stated that OpenAI's first device would be a small, screenless, neck-wearable product equipped with cameras and microphones to capture the user's surroundings, with a smartphone handling computation and display functions."}

{'index': 8, 'translation': 'The company, on the other hand, has hinted at plans to launch multiple devices rather than a single product, and stated in court documents for the iyO case that its first product is not an in-ear or wearable device as speculated when the partnership was announced.'}
